item.title: Tim Curry Gets Ultimate Tribute - Named as an Official Honorary Muppet ...
item.description: https://www.instagram.com/p/Dcgm_DTlIZE/?img_index=1 Few humans have earned the title of honorary Muppet more than the legendary Tim Curry. As a performer he was unparalleled – witty, charming, unnerving, and deeply funny. We will always consider it one of our greatest treasures to have been part of Long John Silver’s crew. Thank you for everything, Tim. Others, including comedians Robin Williams and Pee-Wee Herman are also part of the extremely selective group of human Muppets. In his 2025 memoir “Vagabond,” he describes “Muppet Treasure Island” as “one of the best pictures I ever made” and “most apex of my big films from the 1990s.” The experience was truly life-changing for the actor. “I cannot overstate how much I adored working with the Muppets,” Curry wrote in the book. “The extraordinary thing about them is that they are all characters in their own right, and you should treat them as such.” The film, an adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson’s classic, revolves around the adventures of a young orphan named Jim Hawkins who gets wrapped up in a swashbuckling adventure with Curry’s Long John Silver to find buried treasure. The film, Curry wrote in his memoir, allowed him to tap into his feelings around the death of his own father, who passed away when the actor was 12 years old. “There’s a whole improvised scene where Silver is trying to establish a rapport and relationship between himself and young Jim,” Curry wrote. “Having lost my father at a similar age, and for that to have been such a formative time for me, made my heart go out to Jim’s character in a very authentic way. I tried to imagine how I wished people had spoken to me when I was a boy.” https://www.today.com/popculture/news/tim-curry-honorary-muppet-tribute-rcna594789

item.title: My Poor Kitty
item.description:
My 15 year old Tortoiseshell "Shelly" escaped from the house last Monday morning, and when we finally found her late in the evening she was not usher left hind leg. We rushed her to the emergency vet to get checked out and they found that her upper femur was shattered.
She weirdly was not in much pain, she just wanted to eat and play like normal. But they zooted her up on the good drugs to be sure she was comfortable.
Sadly, they said our only option was amputation. Shelly is over 15 years old, and we were so worried this would be too much for her to handle.
All the vet staff were impressed with Shelly's great attitude, she loves everyone. The whole time she wanted cuddles and belly rubs. While getting assessed, they discovered she had a terrible UTI that showed no symptoms at all. It came up in her blood work and urinalysis. She was just days away from getting really sick. So we were able to start nipping that in the bud.
Nicole (nicnak044) Forbidden lottery numbers 4 5 4 6 2 5 3
Fresh out of surgery as a tripod. Her tail was wrapped to keep it clean. She's on strong pain killers and antibiotics for the next 10 days.
I was so afraid the first few days as she would not eat or drink.
But as of yesterday she is eating and drinking and going on short walks around the house with me! She's using the litter box and acting very normal! We have a cone for her but she has no interest in touching her stitches at all so far!
I have her in a crate to make sure she rests and the other cats don't bother her, so far they only want to comfort her. I set up a camera to keep an eye on here and make sure she is kept safe. This entire ordeal cost us close to $7000, we don't have $7000... So times are going to be very tough for a while. (well, tougher, as it's already been pretty bad lately)
